arguments.request: Add a URL-based notification integration Django view (save VictorOps webhook URL to project)

request: Add the add_victorops view in hc/front/views.py so logged-in users can save a VictorOps webhook URL to their project.

summary.result_text:
I added `add_victorops` to `hc/front/views.py`, but nothing routes to it yet, and I haven't run it or any tests. I only confirmed that `Channel` was already imported and that `require_setting` is now imported at line 55.

The view follows the org's reviewed `integrations.add_url_channel@v1` pattern, with the `# pcat:` marker kept above it:
- It requires `VICTOROPS_ENABLED` and a logged-in user.
- It gets the project through `_get_rw_project_for_user`, so only users with write access can add a channel.
- On a valid POST it validates the URL with `AddUrlForm` and saves a `Channel` of kind `victorops`. It then assigns all checks and redirects to `hc-channels`.
- On a GET, or an invalid POST, it renders `add_victorops.html` with the form.

- **Routing:** `hc/integrations/victorops/urls.py` routes `hc-add-victorops` to `views.add` in `hc/integrations/victorops/views.py`. That file has only imports and no `add` function, so the new view isn't reachable. Either point the URL at `front.views.add_victorops`, or move the view into that module and drop it from `front/views.py`. Say which you'd prefer and I'll make the change.
- **`check_code`:** I ran it before editing, on the snippet alone. It flagged two high-severity deviations (PC100, PC103), saying the function no longer calls `_get_rw_project_for_user` or uses `django`. Both look like artifacts of checking the snippet without its imports, since the body matches the pattern apart from the setting name, channel kind and template name. I didn't re-run it on the final file, and I didn't add any `pcat-allow` lines.
